newsitem.title: CHINA: Deng Xiaoping's widow to attend HK handover.
newsitem.headline: Deng Xiaoping's widow to attend HK handover.

text.p: The widow of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping will witness her late husband's dream come true when Beijing takes back Hong Kong after more than 150 years of British colonial rule.
Zhuo Lin, accompanied by one of her three daughters, Deng Nan, would attend the handover ceremony in Hong Kong at midnight on June 30, state radio said on Tuesday.
Zhuo was listed among the top 18 members of China's delegation to the ceremony together with President and Communist Party chief Jiang Zemin and Premier Li Peng.
She has not been seen in public since state television showed her weeping as she scattered the ashes of her late husband over the sea from a military transport plane.
Zhuo and Deng Nan, who is Vice-Minister of the State Science and Technology Commission, are the only members of the Deng family in the government delegation.

Deng, who transformed China from a backward Stalinist state into a burgeoning economic superpower, had said one of his greatest dreams was to see the handover of Hong Kong -- in a wheelchair if necessary.
He died on February 19, aged 92, after running the world's most populous country for 19 years.
Deng's landmark "one country, two systems" formula to leave Hong Kong untouched for 50 years enabled Britain and China to reach agreement on the transfer of power in 1984.

Deng always refused to visit Hong Kong before the enclave emerged from colonial rule -- although he passed through the territory briefly once in 1929 to avoid capture as a communist by China's then Nationalist government.
